reachable:
Yes, and cleanly. The coding is applied inside collate at training time and reproduced at scoring time by the SAME function: cups_probe.stream_coded_toks calls stream.code_cmds on both arms. I ran the real instrument on the real inner-split context (640 windows) plus a 24-window swap cache with this stream: it passes the prefix-causality replay and the read-token-parity assertion without raising. At the scored read position the token carries code(read_path) in both the SRC and DST blocks, bit-identical between the native and role-swapped arms (structural: the read is not an mv position, and code_cmds is a pure function of the string at that index). The differential information sits where it should — on the mv tokens, where the arms differ by max |diff| 3.0-5.4 per coordinate on real windows. Verified position-wise (permuting the command list permutes the output identically), prefix-causal exactly, and non-mutating of its input. The stream introduces no parameters, so guard_reach is untouched; gradient reaches the mechanism through arch cmd_proj/proj and the head's src_ext/dst_ext. collate is bit-identical to realenv M.collate on types/key_pad/tgt/cmd_mask and on every observation token; exactly 296 coordinates of each command token change and the other 472 are bit-preserved.

One harness note (NOT this candidate's defect, but it should be passed up): on windows with no legal role-swap partner (7 of 24 in my sample), stream_coded_toks codes the native arm but leaves that row of tok2 uncoded, and the read-parity assertion skips exactly those rows (`if cache["swapped_cmds"].get(i) is None: continue`). I measured a 4.73 read-token divergence on fedora:latest:48:19 for that reason. It is harmless today only because cups_ca drops windows absent from the swap rows out of W — the safety of every coding stream rests on that drop, not on the gate whose error text claims to cover it.
solves_outside_model: No. Nothing resolves the move chain. _code_vector(cmd) is a pure function of one command string: it never reads another command, an observation, the future, or any per-sequence state — verified by execution, not by reading (permutation equivariance over a shuffled command list, and exact equality between coding a 7-command prefix and truncating the full-sequence coding). What lands in the token is an ADDRESS — a SHAKE-256 balanced sign code of the command's own first positional argument and its own destination argument, plus a verb code and 8 form flags — all of which are already in the command string in plaintext. Composing 'mv A B; mv B C; cat C' into 'C holds what A held' is left entirely to the network. No position, index, depth or ordinal is encoded, so nothing in the coding supports a first-mover or chain-position heuristic. The scored read token is identical in both arms, so a location-keyed predictor still cancels to exactly zero. This is categorically unlike the retracted +0.9026 stream: no answer is computed anywhere in Python. The batcher (r3) parses mv edges only to compute sequence sampling weights — sample selection, explicitly legitimate. The objective's use of the coded tokens is a training-time similarity gate inside the loss, never an input at scoring.
summary:
The stream mechanism — the axis this slot was assigned — does exactly what its hypothesis says, on every point I could check by execution. I verified: the four disjoint blocks (128 SRC / 128 DST / 32 VERB / 8 FLAG = 296 fixed, command-independent coordinates out of 768); balanced codes summing to exactly 0 with squared norm exactly 288 and mean |cosine| 0.0702 / max 0.375 over the 293 real paths in the sample (author claimed 0.069 / 0.34 on their own 100-path draw); the same generator and tag for both roles, so one path yields one vector in either block; true OVERWRITE semantics, with the other 472 coordinates bit-preserved and coded energy exactly 626 for every command (surviving embedding energy measured at 466.5 against the claimed 472); sibling paths near-orthogonal (0.0 for f385.tmp vs f385.tmp.1) as intended; and collate bit-identical to the harness collate everywhere except those 296 command coordinates. The two corpus facts in section 1 hold: all 172 mv steps have empty output and exit 0 (their rendered observation takes just two constant values, and the hypothesis hedges that correctly), 0 of 966 positional arguments are relative, and 24/24 cups_test read paths are string-identical to an earlier mv destination. The crossover claims about the other axes check out too: r22 does subclass r18 with a zero-init comp_out, and boardpair_swap_difference is WANTS_CTX with _SAME_CMD = 0.999 and its first three terms mathematically verbatim from r12.

Two claims do not survive. The load-bearing one is section 4's justification for keeping the partner's objective: the coding does NOT recover pairs the miner was discarding. On the real pack, distinct long-path commands sit at mean cosine 0.257 with zero fraction above 0.999, and running the objective's own miner on a real batch gives an identical 169 repeat rows / 172 pairs under baseline and under the coding — the 25 pairs the 0.999 gate kills are literally identical command strings in both. The author could not have measured this (no torch in the jail) and stated it as fact. Secondarily, section 1(c)'s 'close to unreadable' overstates: I encoded argument-swapped mv twins with the pinned eye and the order residual is small (standardized cos 0.9795 vs 0.416 between different commands) but a linear probe still reads order at 87.5% on unseen paths — which is failure mode #1 the author themselves listed. Neither affects what the code does, whether it is measurable, or the meaning of the score; both affect the description it will be archived under.

divergences.claim: Section 4: 'Under baseline coding, two different long paths under the same prefix are far above 0.999 similar and the pair miner silently discards them; under my coding ... the miner recovers the pairs it is meant to find.' Presented as the reason boardpair_swap_difference was kept.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The miner's yield is IDENTICAL under baseline and under the coding. It discards nothing that the coding recovers, because distinct commands were never near 0.999 in the first place.
divergences.evidence: Measured on the real pack (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd) with train-split standardization, which is exactly the quantity the miner sees (harness._train passes ctx['cmd'] = stream.extract_cmd_input(b)[m]): distinct 'cat /tmp/w/cups/...' pairs have mean cosine 0.2573, max 0.9958, fraction >= 0.999 = 0.0000; distinct 'mv ...' pairs mean 0.2531, max 0.9986, fraction >= 0.999 = 0.0000. Running the objective's own _repeat_rows/_board_pairs on a real 64-sequence batch: baseline -> 169 repeat rows / 172 pairs / 194 candidate pairs; candidate coding -> 169 / 172 / 194. All 25 candidate pairs killed by the 0.999 gate are literally identical command strings, in BOTH codings (verified by string comparison) — which is what the gate is for. The author had no torch and no embeddings in the jail, so this number could not have been measured.

divergences.claim: Section 1(c): the encoder superposes src and dst so that 'the residual that distinguishes them is tiny', leaving move direction 'close to unreadable from its input'.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The residual is genuinely small in magnitude, but it is NOT unreadable: a plain linear probe recovers argument order on paths it has never seen.
divergences.evidence: Encoded 200 real 'mv A B' commands and their argument-swapped twins with the pinned eye (enc/e5-nocwd). Raw cos(fwd,rev) = 0.9957; standardized cos = 0.9795 (min 0.9517) against mean 0.416 between two genuinely different mv commands, and ||Sf-Sr|| = 5.90 vs mean inter-command distance 31.9 — so the magnitude claim holds. But a ridge-regularized linear probe trained on 140 path-pairs reads order at 87.5% single-example / 93.3% paired accuracy on held-out pairs with unseen paths. The author lists exactly this as failure mode #1 in section 5, so the hypothesis is internally honest; the section-1 framing is simply stronger than the evidence.

divergences.claim: Section 2: 'A single linear map that reads the SRC block and a single linear map that reads the DST block therefore return the identical key for the identical path. That is exactly the invariant the parent's head assumes.'
divergences.what_the_code_does: The coding makes that invariant EXPRESSIBLE, not true. src_ext and dst_ext are independent nn.Linear(768,256) followed by GELU and a shared path_key; they return the same key only if they learn equal weights on their respective blocks. At init dst_ext = src_ext + 0.02 noise, so both read the same coordinates and ks ~= kd for every command — the separation has to be learned.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py lines ~78-90 (dst_ext.weight.copy_(src_ext.weight + noise); shared self.path_key) and the run() body (ks = path_key(gelu(src_ext(c))), kd = path_key(gelu(dst_ext(c)))). SRC_COLS and DST_COLS are disjoint coordinate sets, so a single weight matrix does not automatically read the same code in both roles.
